propositions: The flat per-context bound (_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS=100,000) refuses oversized recovery inputs (c9f7: 121,147 chars) even when the product (context_chars × criteria_count = 2.67M) remains within the ratified worst-case ceiling (32 × 100k = 3.2M)

Two independent ceilings are conflated: physical (context must fit in one model window) and economic (recovery re-sends context once per criterion), causing arbitrary per-axis refusals that block feasible recovery runs

The physical ceiling must derive from the resolved verifier model's own context window (not a flat constant), and the economic ceiling must explicitly model the per-criterion fan-out product, with diagnostic telemetry reporting both

Moving MODEL_LADDER to shared model_classes.py and adding an own-window accessor (distinct from plan-review's escalation-aware largest_window_tokens) unblocks window-derived ceilings without breaking existing plan-review call sites
A context-size-limited Bedrock evidence run (115k chars) completes with a verdict when the physical ceiling is model-derived (2M chars for sonnet) instead of refusing at preflight (100k flat bound)
